title: An education mentor's review reset our positioning
subtitle: 40-minute live demo with an education mentor from Central Square Foundation, 21 Oct. Findings logged in docs/TESTING_LOG.md.
rows: “Second teacher” overclaims: in a noisy room a speaker alone may not solve active learning
Now a classroom companion: it helps the teacher manage groups, and does not replace her
You can claim engagement at this stage, not that learning happened
We claim engagement only. No learning gain is claimed
How does it look in action? The direction must reach the teacher
“Set up the room” before every lesson: teacher with those who need her most, one child as helper, in 4 languages
Grade 1–3 children cannot run the study mode alone; it can serve parents
/tutor is now a labelled prototype parent helper, off the home hero, with a short spoken note for parents
Few features that work beat many. Is the script engaging for a Grade 2 child?
Effort moved back to the classroom loop: five activity types (pebble, slate, pair work, song, story) and teacher controls
Indic models err at scale; launch with a data caveat. Use state teacher guides as input
Not done yet: on the roadmap. Native-speaker sign-off stays a required guardrail
status: This is one expert review, plus the team's own device tests. No teacher or child has used it yet in a real classroom, and no learning outcome has been measured. Teacher sessions with written consent are the first roadmap item.
auditFix: New voice key; packs rebuilt; the five built-in lessons now speak offline; recordings allowed through the body limit
